task_instance: Recreated the skill's bundled setup_env.py and check_versions.py (not present in the ce_sources copy, only SKILL.md/LICENSE were) from the documented behavior, then ran the full workflow: create an isolated .venv pinned to Python 3.12 via uv, install requirements.txt (boto3, awscli) with --upgrade, verify with importlib.metadata-based check_versions.py, confirm idempotency on re-run, confirm version-override/recreation-on-mismatch (.venv 3.11), and confirm the isolated env's boto3 (1.43.103) differs from a pre-existing older boto3 in system Python (1.35.49), demonstrating true isolation.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/huggingface__skills__hf-cloud-python-env-setup. Files: requirements.txt (boto3, awscli), scripts/setup_env.py, scripts/check_versions.py. Commands: `python3 scripts/setup_env.py` created .venv via `uv venv --python 3.12 .venv` then `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --upgrade -r requirements.txt`, output showed 'Installed 13 packages' including boto3==1.43.103, awscli==1.46.1. Re-running the same command printed 'Env already exists at .venv with Python 3.12.3. Skipping creation.' and 'Audited 13 packages' (idempotent, no reinstall). `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_versions.py` printed boto3: 1.43.103 / botocore: 1.43.103 / awscli: 1.46.1 via importlib.metadata.version(); passing an unknown package name printed 'NOT INSTALLED' instead of crashing. `.venv/bin/python --version` -> Python 3.12.3. Running `python3 scripts/setup_env.py .venv 3.11` printed 'Existing env at .venv is Python 3.12.3, not 3.11. Recreating.' and rebuilt with Python 3.11.15, confirmed by `.venv/bin/python --version`; re-running with default args recreated back to 3.12.3, confirming version pin + mismatch detection works both directions. Confirmed isolation: `python3 -c 'import boto3; print(boto3.__version__, boto3.__file__)'` on the system interpreter showed a pre-existing boto3 1.35.49 at /usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages, unaffected by the venv install of 1.43.103 -- i.e. nothing was installed into system Python. No credentials, accounts, or paid/deployed AWS services were needed for this task (only PyPI package downloads over the proxy).
